note: Ranked on impact_sum: the hunters' signed per-finding sizes, added up, in points of spot. No call and no threshold -- cut wherever you like afterwards, which is what keeps the ranking question answerable at every k. `conviction` (abs of the key) is where the direction skill lives: over all events the sign is a coin flip, above the median conviction it is 74%. conviction_floor is a floor on emphasis in the note, never a filter on this file. Everything under `diagnostics` was measured as neutral or subtractive and decides nothing -- see researcher_us/EDGE_ANALYSIS.md.

findings.finding: Chipotle's Q3 2026 8-K/10-Q (filed 2026-10-28, after CAVA last spoke) puts the summer food-safety hit to fast casual at low single digits. The headwind began in July, worsened for several weeks, and was gone by the end of August, when comp trends returned to pre-disruption levels. CMG's Q3 comp was +2.1% against +2.2% in Q2, and its two-year stack improved. Restaurant-level margin pressure into Q3/Q4 with an EBITDA guide to defend. The Q2 restaurant-level margin was 25.7%, down 60bp YoY, with about 100bp of salmon headwind. Management flagged further pressure from fuel surcharges and pre-marinated chicken, plus a seasonal Q4 drop of about 300bp. Q3 also carries deleverage from the weeks of flat SRS during Cyclospora. H1 adjusted EBITDA was $116.4m ($61.7m + $54.7m), so H2 needs $64.6-74.6m to meet the $181-191m guide. A trim to the margin or EBITDA range is the main downside path.

findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Loss-ratio-driven prints: Q2 2025 (2025-08-06) fell 26.4% and Q3 2025 fell 8.8%, the latter on margin pressure (StockStory Q3 2025 deep dive headline). Q2 2026 fell 16.2% despite a flat 66% net loss/LAE ratio.

findings.finding: Root's reported loss ratio is being supported by reserve releases. H1 2026 favorable prior-year development was $28.5M against $14.0M in H1 2025 (Q2 10-Q), and Q2's gross loss ratio of 58.7% sat ~2.9 pts below the 61.6% gross accident-period ratio. If Q3 releases shrink, the reported loss ratio rises even with a stable underlying trend. If they persist, the beat is low-quality, which this stock sold in Q2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: EPS of $1.49 against $0.67 consensus, flattered by PYD and a 26.1% expense ratio; the stock fell 16.2% (baseline 2026-08-05; https://stockunlock.com/investing/root-stock-q2-2026-earnings/).

findings.finding: The Q3 2026 competitive environment for Root's direct channel worsened. Progressive's Q3 advertising rose 18% to $1.6B, its average written premium per personal auto policy fell 2% YoY, and its policy life expectancy fell 9% YoY (more churn). GEICO also resumed heavy advertising. Root guided PIF to 'relatively flat YoY if competitive conditions persist' after PIF fell sequentially from 495,429 to 483,921 in Q2, and Q2 GWP was down 2% YoY. So a further sequential PIF and GWP decline and lower retention are the risk, mostly inside what was guided.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: the flat-PIF guide and the sequential PIF decline were the main reason for the -16.2% reaction (StockStory/StockUnlock). Q1 2026's growth-muted warning still produced +3.4%.

findings.finding: On 2026-08-31 Root and Carvana restructured their partnership: the commercial agreement runs two years to ~2028-08-31 with auto-renewal, exclusivity was rewritten, and deep-OTM 2021 warrants ($180-540 strikes) were swapped for a 1,525,560-share performance warrant. The new warrant has five tranches struck at 130-170% of a $55.72 VWAP and vests at 180k/210k/250k/290k/340k cumulative policies attributed after 2026-08-31. Carvana's Q3 2026 retail units were 217,385, +39% YoY (released 2026-10-28). Partnerships plus agents were ~51% of Root's new writings in Q2, and Carvana had passed 200k lifetime policies by Q1 2026. The milestone ladder implies both sides expect a materially faster attributed-policy run-rate.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Partnership-channel strength was the stated bright spot of Q1 and Q2 2026, but it did not prevent the -16.2% Q2 reaction, so the stock has not paid for this line on its own.

findings.finding: Carvana warrant accounting is an unquantified one-off in Q3 2026. Q3 2025's $5M GAAP net loss included a $17M noncash Carvana warrant expense, so the YoY GAAP comparison is flattered. The 2026-08-31 cancellation and reissue may create a modification charge or contra-revenue in Q3 2026 whose size the filing does not state.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 printed a GAAP loss on the $17M warrant expense and fell 8.8%, but the reaction was attributed to margin and outlook, not the warrant.

findings.finding: Expense ratio normalization was guided. The CFO said Q2's 26.1% net expense ratio is not the new normal, pointed to ~29% (Q1/Q4) as the reference, and expects SBC back at $8-9M a quarter; $10M is allocated to new acquisition channels in H2 2026. Expect Q3 operating income to compress against Q2 on expenses alone, inside what was guided.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This was guided in Q2 and contributed to that -16.2%. Since it is already told, a match should be near zero.

findings.finding: Root had ~$54.2M left on its $75M buyback at 2026-06-30, after $20.8M repurchased in H1, and the stock traded ~$48-54 through Q3: Form 4 tax-withholding prices of $53.60 on 2026-09-15 and $49.78 on 2026-09-21, against a $55.72 VWAP on 2026-08-31. Cash was $509.6M against a market cap of ~$850M. Q3 repurchases at those prices and a possible increased authorization land on the print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The first buyback disclosure, with Q1 results on 2026-05-06, coincided with +3.4%. The >$20M Q2 repurchase did not offset the Q2 sell-off.

findings.finding: Short interest rose 13% in September to 2.08M shares (2026-10-15 settlement), at 12.05 days to cover on ~157k average daily volume. That is ~13.4% of shares outstanding and a larger share of free float. A crowded short on a thin tape, so an in-line or better print with a stable loss ratio has a squeeze mechanism. This partly explains the +15% 20-day run-up.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2025-02-26: +25.6% on a profitability milestone with a heavy short. Shorts were rewarded on the 2025-08-06 (-26.4%) and 2026-08-05 (-16.2%) prints.

findings.finding: Root's next-generation pricing model is due to roll out state by state from late Q4 2026, and New Jersey went live 2026-07-22 (37 states, >80% of the US population, contiguous US targeted by 2027). The Q3 call is the first update on both. A confirmed launch or early NJ volume could support the 2027 growth narrative after the flat-PIF guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 2026 pricing-model announcement with a '2027 impact' did not prevent -16.2%. Product and state-expansion news has not moved this stock on its own.

outside_window.finding: The Carvana warrant tranches can only vest once 180k+ cumulative attributed policies are reported, quarterly within 15 days of quarter end, over a two-year term. The value of the partnership extension resolves over 2027-2028, not on this print.

findings.finding: Rates moved against the capital-cost assumption behind the 2026-08-05 guide cut. The 10-year Treasury was 4.70% on 2026-08-03, when the CFO cut FY Cash Generation to $200-375M partly for 'modestly higher capital costs'. It then rose to 5.00% on 09-15, 5.24% on 09-28 and a 5.31% close on 10-05, and eased to 5.00% on 10-23. Q3 and early Q4 project finance was therefore priced 30-60bp above the guide's rate deck, and an analyst flagged roughly 50bp higher 7-year yields as 'a headwind to 2026 cash generation guidance'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance lines drive this name. The 2026-02-26 print, with the outlook as the focus, went -35.1%. The 2026-08-05 print cut the cash generation and subscriber value guides on a large revenue/EPS beat and went -10.6%.

findings.finding: The FY2026 Cash Generation guide needs an H2 that looks large against everything since the cut. H1 2026 Cash Generation excluding safe harbor was about $14M (Q1 -$31M, Q2 +$45M). Holding the $200-375M guide therefore requires $186-361M in H2. H2 2025 delivered $295M (Q3 $108M, which included a third-party system sale, and Q4 $187M) on Q3 2025 subscriber additions of 30,104. 2026 additions are running 25-31% lower (Q1 17,665, Q2 19,793) and capital costs are higher. The midpoint ($273M H2) needs roughly 2025's H2 on about 30% less volume. The company itself expects direct volume to return to YoY growth in Q3 and grow more than 10% in H2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Same guidance line as above. The Q2 2026 cash-generation cut produced -10.6% despite a 16% revenue beat. Q3 2025 reported $108M of cash generation with the guide unchanged at the midpoint and the stock fell 16.1%.

findings.finding: Counterparties that reported after Sunrun last spoke show US residential demand down sharply. Enphase (2026-10-27) reported Q3 US sell-through -35% YoY and cited third-party data with US residential permits down about 35% YoY in Q3. It guided Q4 sell-through down another 10% sequentially, with Q4 revenue at a $240M midpoint against $298.6M consensus, and its CEO sees 'no meaningful recovery'. SolarEdge (2026-11-04) guided Q4 revenue to $245-275M from $326.1M in Q3, citing 'softer demand'. Enphase is also scaling its own Propel prepaid-lease TPO product: 350 installers and more than 300 weekly originations.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Subscriber additions fell 25% (Q1) and 31% (Q2) YoY. The Q1 print went +7.6% and the Q2 print -10.6%, so the volume line by itself has not set the sign; the guide did.

findings.finding: The print turns on a company-stated volume test: on the Q2 call management said direct-business volume resumes YoY growth in Q3 and grows more than 10% YoY in H2. Affiliate installations are expected down more than 60% for the year (partner Freedom Forever went bankrupt), direct sales are expected to exceed 85% of origination, and more than 1,500 sales reps were hired year to date. Q3 total subscriber additions of about 30,104 in Q3 2025 set the YoY comparison. The direction is undetermined from public data.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Volume misses have come bundled with guide cuts (2026-08-05, -10.6%). A volume line inside the company's own Q3 expectation is a reported-quarter item the market was told to expect.

findings.finding: The short is crowded and the option market leans up into the print. 71.66M shares were short as of the 2026-10-15 settlement (about 29.8% of 240.85M shares outstanding) at 8.6 days to cover, up from 64.7M on 08-19. The 25-delta skew is -28.5 vol points, so calls are richer than puts, and put/call OI is 0.19. The stock ran +19.6% in 5 sessions off a $6.78 52-week low into the print, on 2.3x normal volume today. A print that avoids a cash-generation cut gives a squeeze mechanism with 8.6 days of cover.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The upside reactions on this name are large: +32.3% (2025-08-06), +15.0% (2025-05-07) and +7.6% (2026-05-06), consistent with short covering. But 4 of the last 7 prints fell, by 8-35%.

findings.finding: The reported-quarter bar has been cut. EPS estimates fell more than 20% over the two months to 2026-11-04, and the revenue consensus is about $757-760M against $870M reported in Q2 and $724.6M in Q3 2025. Sunrun beat Q2 revenue by 16% ($870.0M vs $746.9M) and EPS by $0.19, and Q1 by $0.67. A headline beat is the likely outcome, but this name has sold its headline beats.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 beat revenue by 16% and EPS by 83% and the stock went -10.6%. Q3 2025 was reported as 'strong' and went -16.1%. Q1 2026 beat and went +7.6%. Headline beats do not set the sign here.

findings.finding: Grid-services evidence is building. Sunrun's California home batteries delivered a record 745 MW on 2026-10-06 (the prior record was 580 MW on 09-09). Its Puerto Rico distributed power plant doubled to more than 60,000 customers and dispatched for 18 consecutive days from 10-13. This supports the Tesla/Renew Home 16 GW flexible-capacity narrative from June.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The June 2026 Tesla/Renew Home partnership produced a +13-22% day outside a print. Grid-services revenue has not been a print line before.

findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no history of RUN reacting to Tesla storage data at its own print.
